data.claim: Every stage except claim refusals and human wait is derivable from existing events folded by facts.collect.
data.falsifier: A seeded log with known durations whose stage figures differ from the arithmetic, or a stage that needs an event the log lacks.
data.mechanism: facts already holds spans, leases, starts and outcomes; only lease.waiting times, worktree.merged times and diff_stat lines were unread.
data.probe_output: 10 passed in 4.68s (queue 1650, lease 500, implement 300, review_wait 800, merge_wait 300, claim_to_merge 2700 on the seeded log)
data.question: Can the cycle-time split be cut from existing events (lease.waiting, gate.started, gate.* with waited_s and diff_stat, worktree.merged) without a new event kind?

evidence.note: Research Rbed6bd91a9 CONFIRMED: stages derivable from existing events; tests/test_metrics_stages.py 10 passed.

r-small-files: stages.py 10 KB in services/metrics package, service.py only a thin hook; r-reuse-core: facts.collect extended (waits, merges, changed_lines), gate_durations reused; r-everything-configurable: stage_size_small/large knobs plus upgrade notes, README table regenerated; r-no-shell: one declared command gives CLI and MCP; r-tell-dont-discover: answer carries next cli and mcp call; unmeasured stages named not_measured. Deviation: knobs live in [metrics] since no [perf_metrics] section exists yet.
Tests first (tests/test_metrics_stages.py, 10 tests on a seeded log), then stages.py, facts.py, service hook, declared command; ruff check and format clean.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `elif kind == "lease.waiting"` is dead code in the event-folding chain. The branch immediately above it—the one whose body is `_lease_event(facts, span, at, ev, held)`—is the lease-event branch, so it matches `kind.startswith("lease.")` and consumes `lease.waiting` before this new `elif` is reached. Given a log event `kind="lease.waiting"`, `subject="item-1"`, `data={"at": 100.0}`, `_lease_event` runs and the new `facts.waits.setdefault(...)` line never executes, leaving `facts.waits["item-1"]` empty; lease-wait spans are therefore not cut from the timeline as intended.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/facts.py:172

chunk_findings.detail: `has_figures` only inspects `g["stages"]`, but `build` also puts per-gate run/wait statistics in `g["gates"]`. Given `min_samples=5`, one item with five timed runs of a single gate, and no stage statistic meeting the minimum, `_summarise` leaves stage `gate_run` as `p50_s=None` (`n=1`), while `_gate_rows` produces a gate row with `run.n=5` and a non-null `p50_s`. `text` would print that gate figure, but `has_figures(data)` returns `False`, so a caller that uses it to decide whether the view has any figures suppresses figures that are present.
chunk_findings.title: `has_figures`

chunk_findings.detail: When no item has a usable `claim_to_merge` or `cycle_s`, `_gather` leaves `slowest` empty, and `build` emits `next.cli="ddflow metrics retro <item id>"` and `next.mcp="ddflow_metrics view=retro item=<item id>"`. `text` then prints those strings as the next call. For example, one claimed item with a measured `queue_wait` but no merge and `cycle_s=None` produces figures and the line `next: ddflow metrics retro <item id> ...`; that CLI string is not an exact runnable next call, violating the “exact next call” requirement [r-tell-dont-discover].
chunk_findings.title: `build` / `text`

chunk_findings.detail: When `ctx.facts.starts_of(item)` has no start time for a gate outcome, `_first_gate` falls back to the outcome timestamp. Given an item claimed at `0`, no gate start entry, one gate outcome at `10` with duration `10`, and a merge at `10`, `_first_gate` returns `implement=10`, while `_gates` also returns `gate_run=10` from the same outcome duration. The stage split then counts the entire first gate run both as implementation and as gate time, instead of leaving implement unmeasured (or excluding that gate duration) when no gate-start boundary exists.
chunk_findings.title: `_first_gate`

chunk_findings.detail: The seeded timeline makes the asserted “cycle-time split” double-count the same wall-clock intervals. For item A, the test expects `queue_wait` to be 1600 s (task added at `T0 - 1000` to claim at `T0 + 600`) while also expecting `lease_wait` to be 500 s (`lease.waiting` at `T0 + 100` to claim at `T0 + 600`), so the whole lease-wait interval is also counted inside queue wait. It also expects `review_wait` to be 800 s; the only 1300 s span in the seeded log that yields 800 after subtracting the 500 s of review `elapsed_s` is the first rubber-duck failure at `T0 + 2000` through the merge at `T0 + 3300`, which includes the `T0 + 3000`–`T0 + 3300` interval that is separately asserted as `merge_wait` (300 s). Thus the test locks in a split where lease and merge waits are counted twice, so any dashboard or “Little law” analysis that sums stages or attributes parallelism growth will overstate cycle time and misattribute lease waits to queue wait.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_metrics_stages.py:test_each_stage_is_cut_from_existing_events

chunk_findings.detail: The added help documents the new stage-size bounds as `[metrics] stage_size_small/large`, and the manifest’s upgrade file names (`knob_added.metrics.stage_size_large.toml`, `knob_added.metrics.stage_size_small.toml`) confirm they live in `[metrics]`. The change’s own conformance item [r-everything-configurable] requires every threshold and interval to be a knob in `[perf_metrics]` with org lock. Concrete failure: an org that locks `[perf_metrics]` to require approval for threshold changes will not be locking these new thresholds, so a local config can set `[metrics] stage_size_large = 1` and silently change size bucketing; config readers/tooling that look for thresholds under `[perf_metrics]` will not find them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/metrics.md

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `s["review_wait"]["p50_s"] == pytest.approx(800)` is based on an incomplete span. In the seeded log, the research gate passes at T0+1000 and the first rubber_duck review starts at T0+1700 (T0+2000 gate.failed minus `elapsed_s` 300), so the wait for the first review is 700 s. The second review wait from the first rubber_duck verdict at T0+2000 to the second review start T0+2800 is 800 s. Therefore A’s total review wait is 1500 s, not 800. The comment “1300 s span less 500 s reviewing” starts from the first review start and drops the 700 s between the research pass and that first review, leaving part of the timeline unmeasured. A correct implementation that counts all review wait would fail this test; the implementation that passes it under-reports review wait.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_metrics_stages.py:63 (test_each_stage_is_cut_from_existing_events)

chunk_findings.detail: The new boundary can still be guessed from a later gate start when the first gate run has no recorded start. Given an item claimed at `0`, a `gate.passed` for `research` at `10` with `elapsed_s=10` (no `gate.started`), and a `gate.started` for `rubber_duck` at `100`, `ctx.facts.starts_of(...)` returns `[100]`, so `_first_gate` returns `{"implement": 100}`. The first gate actually ended at `10` (or should be left unmeasured because its start is missing); the fold now counts the interval `10..100` as implementation, double-counting gate/review/wait time and inflating the implement stage. The added test only covers the no-start case with no later gate start, so it does not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/stages.py:_first_gate

chunk_findings.detail: The function only considers `ctx.facts.starts_of(span.item)` and picks the minimum recorded start >= first_claim. If the item’s earliest gate run has no `gate.started` event while a later gate run does, the later start is used as the implement boundary, even though the boundary belongs to a later gate. Example: item claimed at T0, research gate passes at T0+10 with `evidence.elapsed_s=10` but no `gate.started`, review gate starts at T0+30. `_first_gate` returns `implement = 30` because the only recorded start is T0+30. The first gate run occurs before T0+30 and its start is unknown, so implement should be unmeasured, not 30; `_gates(runs)` still reports the research run separately, so the split double-counts that run and violates the documented “stage is left unmeasured rather than guessed.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/stages.py:_first_gate

chunk_findings.detail: When `slowest` is empty, `next.cli`/`next.mcp` are changed to a stages view, but the `note` still asserts “the slowest item’s timeline names its biggest gap; regroup with --group-by phase|kind|size|agent”. In the no-slowest case triggered by the new test (one claimed unfinished item), there is no slowest item and the next call is not a retro timeline, so the note is false and misleads callers about what the next call does.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/stages.py:build next.note

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_changed_lines` computes size through `_float`, but `_float` (facts.py:100) returns `None` for `0` because it uses `return float(value) if ok else None` and `ok` is the parsed float value. Given a gate verdict with evidence `{"diff_stat": {"insertions": 0, "deletions": 0}}`, both parts become `[None, None]`, so `_changed_lines` returns `None`. That converts a measured zero-line change into "unknown size" instead of a small size of 0, contrary to the new field doc and the `stage_size_small` doc's unknown/small distinction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/facts.py:_changed_lines

chunk_findings.detail: Outcomes with `waited_s is None` are treated as a zero-length wait. `_gates` computes `waited = [min(o.waited_s or 0.0, d) ...]`, and `_gate_rows` does the same in `run_s = [d - min(o.waited_s or 0.0, d) ...]`. That “or 0.0” converts a missing wait sample into `0.0`, so `gate_run`/per-gate `run` overstate run time, while `gate_wait`/per-gate `wait` omit or understate the unknown wait. For example, one timed gate run with `d=60s` and `waited_s=None` makes `_gates` return `{"gate_run": 60}` and no `gate_wait`, even though the wait was never recorded. The module’s own invariant is that a missing figure is never a zero; it should leave the sample absent and record it as unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/stages.py `_gates` and `_gate_rows`

chunk_findings.detail: The new stage-size bucket thresholds are documented as `[metrics] stage_size_small/large`, and the manifest’s upgrade files are named `knob_added.metrics.stage_size_{small,large}.toml`. That conflicts with the change’s own CONFORMANCE requirement ([r-everything-configurable]) that every threshold/interval be a knob in `[perf_metrics]` with org lock. Concrete failure: a deployment sets the org lock on `[perf_metrics]` and writes `stage_size_small` there; the service reads the unlocked `[metrics]` key instead, so the lock does not govern the threshold and the intended section contract is broken.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/metrics.md:19

chunk_findings.detail: The new stage-size thresholds are declared as `metrics.stage_size_large` and `metrics.stage_size_small`, but the change’s conformance contract requires every threshold and interval to be a knob in `[perf_metrics]` with org lock. When these unreleased notes are folded, the keys will be registered outside the required perf-metrics section; an operator setting `perf_metrics.stage_size_large = 100` will not affect the stages view, and the threshold will escape the required `[perf_metrics]` org-lock boundary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.metrics.stage_size_large.toml:5 (also knob_added.metrics.stage_size_small.toml:5)

In the seeded log, the research gate passes at T0+1000 and the first rubber_duck review starts at T0+1700 (T0+2000 gate.failed minus `elapsed_s` 300), so the wait for the first review is 700 s. The second review wait from the first rubber_duck verdict at T0+2000 to the second review start T0+2800 is 800 s. Therefore A’s total review wait is 1500 s, not 800. The comment “1300 s span less 500 s reviewing” starts from the first review start and drops the 700 s between the research pass and that first review, leaving part of the timeline unmeasured. A correct implementation that counts all review wait would fail this test; the implementation that passes it under-reports review wait.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_metrics_stages.py:63 (test_each_stage_is_cut_from_existing_events)

chunk_findings.detail: The new boundary can still be guessed from a later gate start when the first gate run has no recorded start. Given an item claimed at `0`, a `gate.passed` for `research` at `10` with `elapsed_s=10` (no `gate.started`), and a `gate.started` for `rubber_duck` at `100`, `ctx.facts.starts_of(...)` returns `[100]`, so `_first_gate` returns `{"implement": 100}`. The first gate actually ended at `10` (or should be left unmeasured because its start is missing); the fold now counts the interval `10..100` as implementation, double-counting gate/review/wait time and inflating the implement stage. The added test only covers the no-start case with no later gate start, so it does not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/stages.py:_first_gate

chunk_findings.detail: The function only considers `ctx.facts.starts_of(span.item)` and picks the minimum recorded start >= first_claim. If the item’s earliest gate run has no `gate.started` event while a later gate run does, the later start is used as the implement boundary, even though the boundary belongs to a later gate. Example: item claimed at T0, research gate passes at T0+10 with `evidence.elapsed_s=10` but no `gate.started`, review gate starts at T0+30. `_first_gate` returns `implement = 30` because the only recorded start is T0+30. The first gate run occurs before T0+30 and its start is unknown, so implement should be unmeasured, not 30; `_gates(runs)` still reports the research run separately, so the split double-counts that run and violates the documented “stage is left unmeasured rather than guessed.”

chunk_findings.detail: When `slowest` is empty, `next.cli`/`next.mcp` are changed to a stages view, but the `note` still asserts “the slowest item’s timeline names its biggest gap; regroup with --group-by phase|kind|size|agent”. In the no-slowest case triggered by the new test (one claimed unfinished item), there is no slowest item and the next call is not a retro timeline, so the note is false and misleads callers about what the next call does.

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard only treats a verdict as evidence of an earlier, unstarted gate run when its timestamp is strictly before the first recorded `gate.started`. If the first gate run has no `gate.started` but its verdict lands at the same timestamp as a later gate’s `gate.started`, the function still returns a measured `implement`. For example, seed an item claimed at `T0`, add `gate.passed` for `research` at `T0 + 100` with `evidence={"elapsed_s": 100}` and no `gate.started`, then add `gate.started` for the review gate at `T0 + 100`. `starts_of(...)` gives `first = T0 + 100`, the research outcome is not `< first`, so `_first_gate` returns `{"implement": 100}`. The research run’s elapsed time shows it started at `T0`, so the fold counts the same 100 s both as implementation and as the research gate run; with no recorded start for the first gate run, `implement` should be unmeasured. The added test only covers a verdict strictly before the first start, so it does not answer this case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/stages.py:_first_gate

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard only treats outcomes with `o.at < first` as evidence of an earlier missing-start run. When the missing-start gate's verdict and the first recorded `gate.started` share the same timestamp, the condition is false and `_first_gate` still guesses the implement boundary. Example: item claimed at `T0`, a `gate.passed` for `research` at `T0+100` with `elapsed_s=10` and no `gate.started`, and a `gate.started` for the next gate also at `T0+100`. Then `starts=[T0+100]`, `o.at < first` is false, so `_first_gate` returns `implement=100` while `_gates` also counts the research run as `10` from the same outcome, double-counting the first gate's duration in both implement and gate run. The new test only covers the strictly-earlier case (`T0+10` vs `T0+100`), not the equal-timestamp case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/stages.py:_first_gate

  item    : PM-cycle-split    target: rubber_duck

chunk_findings.detail: The new `elif kind == "lease.waiting"` is dead code in the event-folding chain. The branch immediately above it—the one whose body is `_lease_event(facts, span, at, ev, held)`—is the lease-event branch, so it matches `kind.startswith("lease.")` and consumes `lease.waiting` before this new `elif` is reached. Given a log event `kind="lease.waiting"`, `subject="item-1"`, `data={"at": 100.0}`, `_lease_event` runs and the new `facts.waits.setdefault(...)` line never executes, leaving `facts.waits["item-1"]` empty; lease-wait spans are therefore not cut from the timeline as intended.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/facts.py:172

chunk_findings.detail: `has_figures` only inspects `g["stages"]`, but `build` also puts per-gate run/wait statistics in `g["gates"]`. Given `min_samples=5`, one item with five timed runs of a single gate, and no stage statistic meeting the minimum, `_summarise` leaves stage `gate_run` as `p50_s=None` (`n=1`), while `_gate_rows` produces a gate row with `run.n=5` and a non-null `p50_s`. `text` would print that gate figure, but `has_figures(data)` returns `False`, so a caller that uses it to decide whether the view has any figures suppresses figures that are present.
chunk_findings.title: `has_figures`

chunk_findings.detail: When no item has a usable `claim_to_merge` or `cycle_s`, `_gather` leaves `slowest` empty, and `build` emits `next.cli="ddflow metrics retro <item id>"` and `next.mcp="ddflow_metrics view=retro item=<item id>"`. `text` then prints those strings as the next call. For example, one claimed item with a measured `queue_wait` but no merge and `cycle_s=None` produces figures and the line `next: ddflow metrics retro <item id> ...`; that CLI string is not an exact runnable next call, violating the “exact next call” requirement [r-tell-dont-discover].
chunk_findings.title: `build` / `text`

chunk_findings.detail: When `ctx.facts.starts_of(item)` has no start time for a gate outcome, `_first_gate` falls back to the outcome timestamp. Given an item claimed at `0`, no gate start entry, one gate outcome at `10` with duration `10`, and a merge at `10`, `_first_gate` returns `implement=10`, while `_gates` also returns `gate_run=10` from the same outcome duration. The stage split then counts the entire first gate run both as implementation and as gate time, instead of leaving implement unmeasured (or excluding that gate duration) when no gate-start boundary exists.
chunk_findings.title: `_first_gate`

chunk_findings.detail: The seeded timeline makes the asserted “cycle-time split” double-count the same wall-clock intervals. For item A, the test expects `queue_wait` to be 1600 s (task added at `T0 - 1000` to claim at `T0 + 600`) while also expecting `lease_wait` to be 500 s (`lease.waiting` at `T0 + 100` to claim at `T0 + 600`), so the whole lease-wait interval is also counted inside queue wait. It also expects `review_wait` to be 800 s; the only 1300 s span in the seeded log that yields 800 after subtracting the 500 s of review `elapsed_s` is the first rubber-duck failure at `T0 + 2000` through the merge at `T0 + 3300`, which includes the `T0 + 3000`–`T0 + 3300` interval that is separately asserted as `merge_wait` (300 s). Thus the test locks in a split where lease and merge waits are counted twice, so any dashboard or “Little law” analysis that sums stages or attributes parallelism growth will overstate cycle time and misattribute lease waits to queue wait.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_metrics_stages.py:test_each_stage_is_cut_from_existing_events

chunk_findings.detail: The added help documents the new stage-size bounds as `[metrics] stage_size_small/large`, and the manifest’s upgrade file names (`knob_added.metrics.stage_size_large.toml`, `knob_added.metrics.stage_size_small.toml`) confirm they live in `[metrics]`. The change’s own conformance item [r-everything-configurable] requires every threshold and interval to be a knob in `[perf_metrics]` with org lock. Concrete failure: an org that locks `[perf_metrics]` to require approval for threshold changes will not be locking these new thresholds, so a local config can set `[metrics] stage_size_large = 1` and silently change size bucketing; config readers/tooling that look for thresholds under `[perf_metrics]` will not find them.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `<=` guard is too broad: it treats *any* gate outcome at the first recorded gate start as evidence of an earlier, unstarted gate run, even when that outcome is the first gate's own zero-duration verdict. Seed an item claimed at `T0`, then add `gate.started` for `research` at `T0 + 100` and `gate.passed` for the same `research` gate at `T0 + 100` with `evidence={"elapsed_s": 0}`. There is no earlier gate and the implement boundary is known from the claim and the first gate start (`100` s), but `first` is `T0 + 100`, the same-gate verdict satisfies `span.first_claim <= o.at <= first`, and `_first_gate` returns `{}`; the stages view reports `implement.n == 0` instead of measuring a 100 s implement stage. The guard should suppress only when the verdict actually implies a run that began before `first` (for example via gate identity/elapsed information), not merely when its timestamp equals `first`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/stages.py:105

chunk_findings.detail: The new `<=` makes `_first_gate` treat any gate outcome at exactly the first recorded `gate.started` as proof of an earlier missing-start run, without checking whether that outcome belongs to the gate that started at that timestamp. For an item claimed at `T0`, with `gate.started` for gate `R` at `T0+100` and `gate.passed` for `R` at `T0+100` with `evidence={"elapsed_s": 0}` (a legitimate instant gate), `first=100` and `o.at=100`, so `any(span.first_claim <= o.at <= first)` is true and `_first_gate` returns `{}`. `stages()` then reports `implement` as unmeasured, even though the boundary is known and `implement` should be `100`. The previous `<` condition returned `100` for this input; this change regresses it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/stages.py:105
